key_insight: A three-variable stochastic model explains how stable large-scale circulation supports a relaxational mode and damped oscillatory modes continually excited by turbulence.
engineering_relevance: The model offers a reduced-order framework for understanding coherent circulation, oscillations, and rare flow reversals in buoyancy-driven systems.
method: Derive coupled stochastic equations for circulation angular velocity and a dipolar temperature field from the Boussinesq equations.
Linearize around stable finite-circulation states to identify relaxation and oscillation modes.
Compare predicted modes and Rayleigh-number scalings with thin-disk convection experiments.
evidence_signal: Thin-disk experiments resolve the relaxational and oscillatory modes and show their predicted Rayleigh-number scalings.
watch_item: Validation described in the abstract is limited to a thin-disk cell; applicability to other geometries and quantitative prediction of rare transitions need further testing.
paper_title: Stable eigenmodes of the Large-scale circulation in Turbulent Convection
